source.text:
8. And a plane angle is the inclination of the lines to
one another, when two lines in a plane meet one another,
and are not lying in a straight-line.

source_claims.source_quote: the inclination of the lines to one another
source_claims.requirement: Represent the inclination/angle concept and justify the meaning of its encoding.
Preserve two participating lines and their common-plane condition, explicitly or by a justified ambient-model restriction.
Bind the meeting condition to those same participating lines.

source_claims.source_quote: are not lying in a straight-line
source_claims.requirement: Preserve the joint not-in-a-straight-line condition; do not read it as requiring each side individually to be non-straight.

interpretation_decisions.question: Definition 9 separately introduces rectilinear angles: may definition 8 be restricted to straight constituent lines? Resolve before certification.
Is inclination represented as an angle object, an equivalence class, or a numeric quantity? State the intended invariances.
If a raw determinant is used, is it only a non-collinearity test or claimed to measure inclination? Explain dependence on chosen points along the same sides.

review_failure_probes: A two-line structure without its required incidence/angle conditions is not automatically a source-faithful angle.
A predicate defined separately but never connected to the exported angle interface may leave source conditions unused.
machine_pass_policy: unchanged; this draft never overrides an existing kernel score
